findings.title: enableSqlExpressions always returns false, making the SQL feature flag dead
findings.body: The helper initializes `enabled` to the negation of `h.features.IsEnabledGlobally(FlagSqlExpressions)`, then returns false both when `enabled` is true and when it is false. As a result, every QueryTypeSQL is rejected before parsing regardless of whether the `sqlExpressions` feature toggle is on. If the toggle is meant to control the feature, this should return `h.features.IsEnabledGlobally(...)`; if the feature is intentionally unconditional-off, the function should just return false and not consult the toggle. The current code leaves a contradictory, dead toggle.

findings.title: Original DuckDB json_serialize_sql command construction is still present
findings.body: TablesList still interpolates user SQL into `SELECT json_serialize_sql('%s')` after only replacing single quotes and passes it to RunCommands. The new stub RunCommands returns not implemented so the command is not executed today, but the DuckDB-specific parsing path that carried the original RCE/LFI vector remains wired into NewSQLCommand. Any future real DB implementation or alternate caller would re-enable the vulnerable path. The fix would be safer if this serialization logic were removed rather than only stubbed.

findings.title: No automated tests cover the SQL-expression disabling
findings.body: This security fix adds a hard rejection for QueryTypeSQL and replaces DuckDB with stubs, but no tests are included. There is no check that ReadQuery rejects SQL expressions with the intended error, that NewSQLCommand and sql.TablesList return not-implemented errors, or that the feature flag behavior is as intended. A future regression could remove or invert this guard without CI noticing.
